\begin{quote}
\textbf{Negative Externalities:} Two firms are located adjacent to one another, and each imposes an external cost on the other: the detergent that firm 1 uses in its laundry business makes the fish that firm 2 catches in the lake taste funny, and the smoke that firm 2 uses to smoke its caught fish makes the clothes that firm 1 hangs out to dry smell funny. As a consequence each firm's profits are increasing in its own production and decreasing in the production of its neighbor. In particular if \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) are the firms' production levels then their per-period (stage-game) profits are given by \(v_1(q_1, q_2) = (30 - q_2)q_1 - q_1^2\) and \(v_2(q_1, q_2) = (30 - q_1)q_2 - q_2^2\).

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Draw the firms' best-response functions and find the Nash equilibrium of the stage-game. How does this compare to the Pareto-optimal stage-game profit levels?
\item
  For which levels of discount factors can the firms support the Pareto-optimal level of quantities in an infinitely repeated game?
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
